newsitem.title: UK: Next shares jump on current trade relief.
newsitem.headline: Next shares jump on current trade relief.

text.p: Shares in retailer Next Plc were sharply higher on Friday after the company announced that it had maintained strong sales growth in the first fourteen weeks of the spring/summer season.
The shares leapt 32-1/2p or 4.68 percent to 726-1/2p after earlier setting a new twelve-month high of 732p.
"The shares bounced on relief that current sales growth hadn't slowed," one trader said.
Two leading analysts who declined to be named, said they would not be revising their current year profit forecasts on the back of the trade update however.

Next chairman Lord Wolfson said in March this year that Spring/Summer sales were up 19 percent year on year for Next Retail whilst Next Directory showed sales growth of 38 percent. Overall, sales rose by 24 percent.
Earlier on Friday Next reported at its annual general meeting that in the first 14 weeks of the Spring/Summer season, all these increases had been maintained.
